static_traits.name: Roland
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with colleagues due to negative self-perception; has supportive friends and family, but has not yet discussed work-related insecurity with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past and no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Good cooperativeness, able to clearly express negative automatic thoughts and emotions; rather negative tone, with absolutist wording (e.g. 'I must have done something wrong' 'I am not suited for this job'); willing to try reality testing and explore other interpretations in counseling

basic_info.main_problem: Because students do not come to me for help, I feel like a terrible psychologist.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of inadequacy are affecting my confidence and work performance; I want to understand why I feel this way and what I can do to change.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether students visit and give positive feedback

special_situations.event: A noticeable drop in student visit numbers over several months
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If students do not actively seek my help, it means I am not trusted and my ability is insufficient
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proactively runs group counseling, distributes anonymous questionnaires, and holds coffee chats to prove they are useful
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not trust me, and may even dislike me; I must have done something wrong

special_situations.event: Not having received student feedback on work for a long time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there is no positive feedback, my work has no value and I am terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly waits for or collects feedback to confirm self-worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not needed; my work has no meaning

special_situations.event: The new strategies (groups, questionnaires, coffee chats) have low participation, and feedback is mostly neutral or silent
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If engagement is low, the strategy has failed; I am not suited for this job
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly switching and doubling down on strategies to boost engagement
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: See, I am not suited for this profession; I may have chosen the wrong career path

special_situations.event: Recalling being thanked by students in the past but lacking similar feedback recently
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only continuous thanks and visits prove competence; occasional successes do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittling and negating past positive feedback to maintain the current negative self-schema
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That was just luck or student politeness; it does not mean I am truly capable

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be trusted and recognized by students, feeling one's work is meaningful and truly helps others
core_conflict.fear: Fear of not being needed, of being rejected, and of proving oneself worthless/incompetent
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of security by pursuing external feedback and constantly doubling down on strategies, avoiding facing the 'worthless/failure' self-feeling

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When students do not visit or feedback goes silent
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to interpret external silence as negation of one's ability, believing students distrust or dislike them (transference: projecting self-criticism as others' negative views)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use absolutist, generalized self-deprecation statements (e.g. 'I am not suited for this job'), in a low tone; reduce exploration of other situational factors, emphasizing 'It is all my fault'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reminded of or recalling past student thanks and positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Explaining positive experiences as 'luck' or 'politeness', in order to maintain the stability of the negative self-schema
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Negating positive evidence in a flat but stubborn tone, using expressions like 'that was just luck/they were just being polite', avoiding deeply feeling the value of positive experiences.

manifestations: Feeling at work 'I have not made an impact' 'like wasting time'
Fewer student visits and lack of feedback make them doubt the value and meaning of their work
outcomes: Low mood and an enhanced sense of frustration

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Interpreting students' not visiting and silence as their 'distrust/dislike of me'
Attributing the inner experience of self-denial to external judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism (e.g. 'I am not suited for this job')
Quickly blaming insufficient personal ability when facing low engagement

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating 'should keep receiving student visits and positive feedback' as the sole standard of ability and worth
Developing the rigid inner rule 'if there is no feedback, I am not capable'

exception_events.target_problem: When students visit less or feedback is lacking, Roland typically engages in self-denial, believing himself incompetent, leading to poorer work performance and decreased confidence
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last year received student thanks and positive feedback, experiencing that his intervention was effective and needed
exception_events.reason: Clue: at the time there was direct positive feedback and clear student responses, making it easier to see the value and effectiveness of his work

exception_events.target_problem: After rolling out a new strategy, Roland usually interprets low engagement as 'his own ability being insufficient', further fueling self-doubt
exception_events.unique_outcome: Some students did join group counseling (though not many), showing it was not completely ineffective
exception_events.reason: Clue: some participation and response still exist, providing concrete evidence to revise the 'all-or-nothing' conclusion

positive_force: Proactively tries various outreach strategies (groups, questionnaires, coffee chats)
Holding a Master's degree in psychology and a professional position
Has had success experiences and direct positive feedback
Has a supportive network of friends and family
negative_force: Over-reliance on external validation, tending to negate positive evidence
Cognitive biases such as mind reading and overgeneralization reinforcing self-doubt
Self-criticism intensifies, affecting work performance and colleague relationships
Not yet communicating work insecurity with the support system, leading to a subjective sense of isolation

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-denial and sense of failure in work settings (e.g. 'I am a terrible psychologist' 'I am not suited for this job')
antecedent: Lacking or not yet receiving positive feedback
New strategies have low engagement; feedback is neutral or silent
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalizing external silence and low engagement, over-relying on external validation, and using overgeneralizing, mind-reading cognitive styles
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and anxiety through self-blame and negative conclusions, seeking a seemingly certain interpretation and sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-confidence, damaged work performance, tense relationships with colleagues, leisure and interest activities affected, persistent negative emotions
